newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsui Engineering expects incinerator plant order.
newsitem.headline: Mitsui Engineering expects incinerator plant order.

text.p: Mitsui Engineering & Shipbuilding Co Ltd said on Wednesday that it expects to win a contract to build a next-generation garbage incinerator plant from a group of local governments in western Japan.
The leading shipbuilder expects to receive the order for the plant, which will have a disposal capacity of 220 tonnes per day, by mid-July, a spokesman said.
Operations are due to start around 2001, he said.
The spokesman would not reveal the value of the contract, but said that a garbage incinerator of that size would generally cost around 14 billion yen.
The dioxin emission level from the new plant will meet government guidelines which restrict dioxin emissions from incinerators to less than 0.1 nanogram per one cubic metre.
Dioxin is a highly toxic by-product of some industrial processes and is known to cause a wide range of diseases, including cancer.
The technology of the new plant was introduced from Siemens AG, the spokesman said.
The plant is expected to be partly subsidised by the central government, the spokesman said.
